title: Sets
summary: A [[set|set]] is a collection of numbers or objects. A [[venn-diagram|Venn diagram]] shows how two sets overlap, and set notation names each part: the [[intersection|intersection]], the [[union|union]] and the [[complement|complement]]. Extended adds three sets, [[subset|subsets]] and harder regions.

goals.text: List a set's [[element|elements]] from a description, and count them with $n(A)$.
Use the [[universal-set|universal set]] and complete a two-set Venn diagram.
Find $A \cap B$, $A \cup B$ and $A'$, and solve counting problems with a Venn diagram.
Use $\in$, $\notin$, the [[empty-set|empty set]] and [[subset|subsets]], and sets of points on a line.
Shade and count harder regions, including Venn diagrams with three sets.

before.prompt: How many prime numbers are there between $20$ and $30$?
before.hint: Test each odd number from $21$ to $29$ for factors.
before.explain: $23$ and $29$ are prime. $21 = 3 \times 7$, $25 = 5 \times 5$ and $27 = 3 \times 9$. Revise it in {{lesson:1.1}}.

before.prompt: Which list gives all the multiples of $7$ between $20$ and $50$?
before.explain: $7 \times 3 = 21$ up to $7 \times 7 = 49$. The next one, $56$, is too big. Revise it in {{lesson:1.1}}.

blocks.statement: A set is a collection of objects. Each object in it is an element of the set. You list the elements inside curly brackets: $A = \{2, 4, 6, 8\}$.

blocks.text: Order does not matter, and each element is listed once. So $\{6, 2, 4, 8\}$ is the same set as $A$.

You can also describe a set in words: $B = \{\text{square numbers}\}$. Or use a rule: $\{x : x \text{ is a natural number}\}$ is every $x$ that is a [[natural-number|natural number]]. Read the colon as "such that".
$C = \{x : 2 \leqslant x \leqslant 6\}$ is every number from $2$ to $6$, including $2$ and $6$. When the question also says $x$ is an [[integer|integer]], $C = \{2, 3, 4, 5, 6\}$.
$n(A)$ means the number of elements in $A$. For $A = \{2, 4, 6, 8\}$, $n(A) = 4$. It is a count, not a set.

blocks.question: $P = \{x : x \text{ is an integer and } -3 \leqslant x < 2\}$. List the elements of $P$.
steps: $\leqslant$ means $-3$ is included. $<$ means $2$ is not.
Count up in ones from $-3$, stopping before $2$: $-3, -2, -1, 0, 1$.
Write them in curly brackets.

blocks.question: $F = \{\text{factors of } 45\}$. Find $n(F)$.
steps: Find the factors in pairs: $1 \times 45$, $3 \times 15$, $5 \times 9$.
Count the elements. $n(F)$ is that number, not the list.

check.hint: Test each odd number. Cross out those ending in $5$.

blocks.prompt: Which set is $\{x : x \text{ is an integer and } -1 < x \leqslant 3\}$?

blocks.text: Extended also uses $\in$ for "is an element of" and $\notin$ for "is not an element of". So $4 \in A$, but $5 \notin A$.

sections.heading: The universal set and Venn diagrams

blocks.statement: The universal set, $\mathscr{E}$, is the set of every element the question is about.
blocks.plain: Everything you are allowed to use.

blocks.text: A Venn diagram draws $\mathscr{E}$ as a rectangle and each set as a circle inside it. Elements in both sets go in the overlap. Elements in neither set go inside the rectangle but outside both circles.
To complete one: 1. List each set. 2. Put the elements in both sets in the overlap first. 3. Fill the rest of each circle. 4. Put everything left outside the circles.

blocks.question: $\mathscr{E} = \{x : x \text{ is an integer and } 30 \leqslant x \leqslant 40\}$, $T = \{\text{multiples of } 3\}$ and $V = \{\text{multiples of } 5\}$. Complete a Venn diagram for $T$ and $V$. Then list the elements outside both circles.
steps: $30$ is in both, so it goes in the overlap, once.
The rest of $T$ is $33, 36, 39$. The rest of $V$ is $35, 40$.
Every other element of $\mathscr{E}$ goes outside both circles.
Check: $1 + 3 + 2 + 5 = 11$, and $\mathscr{E}$ has $11$ elements, so nothing is missing or repeated.

blocks.alt: Venn diagram. The rectangle is the universal set, the integers from 30 to 40. Circle T holds the multiples of 3 and circle V the multiples of 5. The overlap holds 30. T only holds 33, 36 and 39. V only holds 35 and 40. Outside both circles are 31, 32, 34, 37 and 38.
blocks.caption: Each element of $\mathscr{E}$ appears exactly once.

blocks.text: Sometimes a region shows a number instead. Then it is how many elements are in that region, not an element.

blocks.question: In a Venn diagram of the members of a club, $S$ is the set who swim and $R$ is the set who run. The regions show: $S$ only $24$, both $13$, $R$ only $19$, and outside both circles $10$. How many members swim?
steps: The swimmers are everyone in circle $S$: the $S$ only part and the overlap.
Add those two regions: $24 + 13 = 37$.
Don't forget the overlap. The $13$ who swim and run still swim.

check.prompt: For the same club, find $n(\mathscr{E})$, the number of members.
check.hint: Add every region, including the one outside the circles.
check.explain: $24 + 13 + 19 + 10 = 66$. The $10$ outside both circles are members too.

blocks.prompt: $\mathscr{E} = \{x : x \text{ is an integer and } 16 \leqslant x \leqslant 25\}$, $A = \{\text{even numbers}\}$ and $B = \{\text{square numbers}\}$. Which elements go in the overlap?
blocks.hint: First list $B$. Which of those are even?
blocks.explain: $B = \{16, 25\}$. Only $16$ is also even, so only $16$ goes in the overlap.

blocks.statement: The intersection $A \cap B$ is the set of elements in both $A$ and $B$.
The union $A \cup B$ is the set of elements in $A$ or $B$ or both.
The complement $A'$ is the set of elements of $\mathscr{E}$ that are not in $A$.

blocks.text: To remember them: $\cap$ looks like an n, for "in both". $\cup$ is a cup that holds everything from both circles.

blocks.alt: Three Venn diagrams, each with sets A and B inside a rectangle for the universal set. Left: only the overlap of the circles is shaded, A intersection B. Middle: both whole circles are shaded, A union B. Right: everything outside circle A is shaded, A complement.
blocks.caption: The shaded region is $A \cap B$, then $A \cup B$, then $A'$.

blocks.question: Use the Venn diagram of $T$ and $V$ from the last section. List the elements of $T \cup V$.
steps: $T \cup V$ is everything inside either circle.
From $T$: $30, 33, 36, 39$. From $V$: $35, 40$. The $30$ in the overlap is listed once.
For comparison, $T \cap V = \{30\}$, only the overlap.

check.prompt: Using the same diagram, which set is $V'$?
check.hint: $V'$ is every element of $\mathscr{E}$ that is not inside circle $V$.
check.explain: Remove $30$, $35$ and $40$ from $\mathscr{E}$. The $T$ only elements $33, 36, 39$ are outside $V$, so they are in $V'$.

blocks.text: Many questions give totals, not elements. Find the overlap first. Two circle totals added together count the overlap twice.

blocks.question: In a class of $32$ students, $18$ are in the drama club ($D$) and $13$ are in the music club ($M$). $7$ students are in neither club. How many students are in both clubs?
steps: Students in at least one club: $32 - 7 = 25$.
Adding the two clubs gives $18 + 13 = 31$. This counts the students in both clubs twice.
So the number in both is the extra: $31 - 25 = 6$.
Fill the diagram to check: $D$ only $18 - 6 = 12$, $M$ only $13 - 6 = 7$, outside $7$. And $12 + 6 + 7 + 7 = 32$.

blocks.text: Writing $18$ and $13$ in the parts outside the overlap counts the $6$ twice. Put the overlap in first, then subtract it from each total.

blocks.prompt: On a Venn diagram of sets $A$ and $B$, which region is $A'$?
blocks.hint: $A'$ is everything in $\mathscr{E}$ that is not in $A$.

options.text: Only the overlap of the two circles
Everything outside circle A, including the part of B outside A
Only the region outside both circles

blocks.explain: The part of $B$ outside $A$ is not in $A$, so it is in $A'$ as well.

verify.truth: Everything outside circle A, including the part of B outside A

blocks.prompt: $n(\mathscr{E}) = 50$, $n(P) = 23$, $n(Q) = 16$ and $n(P \cap Q) = 4$. How many elements are in neither $P$ nor $Q$?
blocks.hint: Find $n(P \cup Q)$ first. Count the overlap once.
blocks.explain: $P$ only $19$, overlap $4$, $Q$ only $12$. So $n(P \cup Q) = 35$, and $50 - 35 = 15$.

sections.heading: The empty set, subsets and sets of points

blocks.statement: The empty set, $\varnothing$, is the set with no elements, so $n(\varnothing) = 0$.

blocks.text: When $A \cap B = \varnothing$, the sets share no elements. Draw their circles apart, with no overlap.

blocks.statement: $A$ is a subset of $B$, written $A \subseteq B$, when every element of $A$ is also in $B$. If even one element of $A$ is not in $B$, write $A \nsubseteq B$.

blocks.alt: Venn diagram for a subset. Inside the rectangle for the universal set, circle A, shaded, lies completely inside the larger circle B.
blocks.caption: $A \subseteq B$: draw circle $A$ inside circle $B$.

blocks.text: Every set is a subset of itself. The empty set $\varnothing$ is a subset of every set, because it has no element that could be missing.

blocks.question: $\mathscr{E} = \{x : x \text{ is an integer and } 1 \leqslant x \leqslant 20\}$, $H = \{\text{multiples of } 6\}$ and $K = \{\text{multiples of } 3\}$. Explain why $H \subseteq K$. Then list the elements of $K \cap H'$.
steps: Each multiple of $6$ is $3 \times 2 \times$ something, so it is a multiple of $3$. So every element of $H$ is in $K$, and $H \subseteq K$.
$K \cap H'$ is the elements of $K$ that are not in $H$.

blocks.text: A set can hold points. $\{(x, y) : y = mx + c\}$ is every point on the line $y = mx + c$. The intersection of two such sets is the points on both lines.

blocks.question: $L = \{(x, y) : y = 3x - 1\}$ and $M = \{(x, y) : y = x + 5\}$. Find the element of $L \cap M$.
steps: A point in both sets lies on both lines, so its $y$-values are equal: $3x - 1 = x + 5$.
Subtract $x$ and add $1$: $2x = 6$, so $x = 3$.
Then $y = 3 + 5 = 8$. Check in $L$: $3 \times 3 - 1 = 8$.
So $L \cap M = \{(3, 8)\}$, a set with one element.

blocks.text: Writing $\{0\}$ or $0$ for the empty set. $\{0\}$ has one element, the number $0$. The empty set is $\varnothing$ or $\{\,\}$.

blocks.prompt: $A = \{3, 7, 10\}$ and $B = \{\text{odd numbers}\}$. Which statement is true?
blocks.hint: Test every element of $A$. One failure is enough.

options.text: A is a subset of B, because 3 and 7 are odd
A is not a subset of B, because 10 is not odd
A is not a subset of B, because B has more elements

blocks.explain: $10 \in A$ but $10 \notin B$, so $A \nsubseteq B$. Size alone never decides it.

verify.truth: A is not a subset of B, because 10 is not odd

blocks.prompt: $\mathscr{E} = \{x : x \text{ is an integer and } 11 \leqslant x \leqslant 15\}$, $E = \{\text{even numbers}\}$ and $D = \{\text{odd numbers}\}$. Which set is $E \cap D$?
blocks.hint: Can a number be both odd and even?
blocks.explain: $E = \{12, 14\}$ and $D = \{11, 13, 15\}$. No number is both, so $E \cap D = \varnothing$. Draw $E$ and $D$ as separate circles.

blocks.text: Build a region in steps. Picture each part shaded. $\cap$ keeps only what both parts share. $\cup$ keeps everything in either part. A $'$ swaps shaded and unshaded.

blocks.alt: Three Venn diagrams with sets A and B. Left: circle A without the overlap is shaded, A intersection B complement. Middle: only the region outside both circles is shaded, A union B, all complemented. Right: everything except the part of A outside B is shaded, A complement union B.
blocks.caption: $A \cap B'$, then $(A \cup B)'$, then $A' \cup B$.

blocks.question: $n(A) = 17$ and $n(A \cap B) = 6$. Find $n(A \cap B')$.
steps: $B'$ is everything outside circle $B$.
$A \cap B'$ is the part of $A$ outside $B$: the "$A$ only" region.
Take the overlap away from all of $A$: $17 - 6 = 11$.

blocks.text: With three sets, fill from the centre out: first the part in all three, then each pair's remaining overlap, then each set alone, then outside.

blocks.alt: Venn diagram with three overlapping circles A, B and C inside a rectangle. The numbers of elements are: A only 7, B only 4, C only 9, A and B only 3, A and C only 5, B and C only 2, all three 6, and outside all three circles 8.
blocks.caption: Each number is how many elements are in that region.

blocks.question: Use the three-set Venn diagram above. Find $n(B' \cap C)$.
steps: $B' \cap C$ is the part of circle $C$ that is outside circle $B$.
Inside $C$ but outside $B$ are two regions: $C$ only ($9$) and $A$ and $C$ only ($5$).
Leave out the $2$ and the $6$: those regions are inside $B$.

check.prompt: Using the same diagram, find $n(A \cap B)$.
check.hint: $A \cap B$ includes the centre, where all three overlap.
check.explain: $A$ and $B$ only is $3$, and the centre is $6$. Both are in $A$ and in $B$, so $3 + 6 = 9$.

blocks.prompt: Using the same diagram, find $n((A \cup B)')$.
blocks.hint: Which regions are outside both circle $A$ and circle $B$?
blocks.explain: Outside $A$ and $B$ are $C$ only ($9$) and outside all three ($8$). So $9 + 8 = 17$.

blocks.prompt: On a two-set Venn diagram, which region is $(A \cup B)'$?

options.text: Only the overlap of the two circles
Only the region outside both circles

blocks.explain: $A \cup B$ is both whole circles. Its complement is what is left: the region outside both.

verify.truth: Only the region outside both circles

blocks.text: $A \cap B$: in both. $A \cup B$: in $A$ or $B$ or both. $A'$: in $\mathscr{E}$ but not in $A$.
$n(A)$ is the number of elements in $A$: a count, not a set.
Venn diagram: fill the overlap first. Every element of $\mathscr{E}$ appears once, including those outside the circles.
$\varnothing$ has no elements. $A \subseteq B$ means every element of $A$ is in $B$.
Three sets: fill the centre, then each pair, then each set alone, then outside.

mistakes: Shading only the overlap for $A \cup B$. The union is both whole circles; the overlap alone is $A \cap B$.
Giving a set such as $\{4\}$ when asked for $n(\ldots)$. Give the number of elements: here $1$.
Putting an element that is in both sets in one circle only, or in a circle and the overlap. It goes in the overlap, once.
Leaving out the elements of $\mathscr{E}$ that are in neither set. They go inside the rectangle, outside the circles.
Writing the circle totals straight into the "only" regions. Subtract the overlap first, or it is counted twice.
Counting the elements of $B$ when asked for $n(B')$. The complement is everything in $\mathscr{E}$ outside $B$.
examTips: "Complete the Venn diagram": every element of $\mathscr{E}$ must appear exactly once. Before moving on, check that the regions add up to $n(\mathscr{E})$.
"Write down $n(\ldots)$": the answer is a single whole number. No working is needed, but read the region carefully.
"List the elements": use curly brackets and write each element once, in any order.
"Shade the region": shade that region only. For a harder region, shade each part lightly in pencil first, then combine.
